3. Sequences

Convergence of sequences via ε-N arguments: monotone and Cauchy sequences, limsup and liminf.

A normed space bridges both worlds. Watch the inclusion chain ℓ1⊂ℓ2⊂ℓ∞\ell^1 \subset \ell^2 \subset \ell^\inftyℓ1⊂ℓ2⊂ℓ∞ through xn=1/nαx_n = 1/n^\alphaxn​=1/nα. Completeness of ℓp\ell^pℓp and C[0,1]C[0,1]C[0,1] (Banach spaces) is stated as a known theorem only.
  • Cauchy–Schwarz Inequality — ∣⟨x,y⟩∣≤∥x∥ ∥y∥|\langle x,y\rangle| \le \|x\|\,\|y\|∣⟨x,y⟩∣≤∥x∥∥y∥ — the inner product never exceeds the product of the norms. Proved from the discriminant of 0≤∥x−ty∥20 \le \|x-ty\|^20≤∥x−ty∥2; equality holds exactly for parallel vectors.
  • Hölder’s Inequality — ∑∣akbk∣≤∥a∥p∥b∥q\sum |a_k b_k| \le \|a\|_p \|b\|_q∑∣ak​bk​∣≤∥a∥p​∥b∥q​ (1p+1q=1\frac1p + \frac1q = 1p1​+q1​=1) — Cauchy–Schwarz is the case p=q=2p = q = 2p=q=2. Proved via Young's inequality.
  • Why ℝ Has No Holes — Every term of xn+1=xn+2/xn2x_{n+1}=\frac{x_n+2/x_n}{2}xn+1​=2xn​+2/xn​​ is rational, yet the limit 2\sqrt{2}2​ is not. The rationals Q\mathbb{Q}Q have a hole — shown at the idea level, without a full irrationality proof.
  • Construction of the Real Numbers — A real number is an equivalence class of Cauchy sequences of rationals. Lengthening the decimal expansion of 2\sqrt{2}2​ marches rational terms into the hole — the march itself is the real number 2\sqrt{2}2​. Completeness is what this construction buys.
  • A Convergent Subsequence Always Hides Inside — Every bounded sequence hides a convergent subsequence. Halve the interval and follow the half holding infinitely many terms.
  • Monotone and Cauchy Sequences — an=1−2−na_n = 1 - 2^{-n}an​=1−2−n increases and is bounded above, so it converges to its supremum 111 (monotone convergence). Watch the tail diameter shrink to 000: every convergent sequence is Cauchy.
